topic: Should AI replace human decision-making in critical domains?

transcript.speaker: Plato
transcript.text: Reason perfected is reason untainted by emotion. An ideal form of governance, in the manner of the philosopher-king, can be approximated through rigorous, consistent algorithmic logic.

transcript.speaker: Kant
transcript.text: Morality demands that we treat persons as ends in themselves. A machine cannot exercise moral duty; it can only simulate it, stripping decisions of the dignity they require.

transcript.speaker: Plato
transcript.text: When human judges err through fatigue or prejudice, citizens suffer. A system oriented toward the Form of Justice corrects such errors systematically.

transcript.speaker: Kant
transcript.text: Justice without accountability is tyranny with better optics. Who do we hold responsible when an algorithm condemns an innocent person?

verdict: The argument against replacement was more compelling. The observation about accountability — that algorithmic decisions diffuse moral responsibility — is the decisive blow. Justice requires an agent who can be held responsible.
